title: Renewal Intervention Runbook — Staged Scenarios & Exec Escalation Scripts
summary: A working runbook for detecting renewal risk early, mapping accounts to staged intervention plays, and providing ready-to-send exec escalation scripts and mitigation tactics geared toward mid-market and enterprise customers.
audience: CS AEs, CSMs, CS Ops, Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success Leadership
purpose: Standardize how we assess renewal risk, align stakeholders, and execute tailored save plays with timelines, escalation points, and measurable outcomes to reduce last-minute robot-saves and increase predictable renewals.
overview: This doc captures a staged approach to renewal interventions: 1) signal detection and triage, 2) account-level play selection, 3) operational run steps, 4) executive escalation scripts, and 5) post-save follow-up and QBR integration. It's intentionally pragmatic with templates and step-by-step actions for each risk tier.
risk-tiers: Tier 0 - Green: Low risk. Healthy usage, adoption signals steady, NPS>30, no exec churn indicators.
Tier 1 - Monitor: Early warning. Declining weekly active usage (-10%+ over 30 days), missed feature adoption milestones, at least one support friction >= Sev2. Begin light-touch remediation.

Tier 2 - Elevated: Clear risk. Contract renewal in <90 days plus declining usage (-25%+), multiple support escalations, key stakeholder turnover, or margin compression. Initiate medium-touch mitigation and stakeholder alignment.

Tier 3 - Critical: At-risk. Renewal <30 days, non-response to CSM outreach, executive concerns voiced, or product/regulatory blockers. Trigger immediate cross-functional play and exec escalation within 48 hours.

Tier 4 - Churn-imminent: Renewal in <14 days with cancel signals (procurement stalls, legal objections without remedies, spend reduction requests). Deploy survival/exit and winback options while engaging legal and sales.
decision-matrix: Matrix (quick reference): Tier 0 = QBR + standard prep; Tier 1 = CSM-led adoption drive + in-product nudges; Tier 2 = AE+SE engagement, executive briefing scheduled, tailored ROI report; Tier 3 = CS Leader + Sales + Product war room, escalation email to customer execs, limited-time incentives (discounts, migration support); Tier 4 = Legal & Finance review, prepare offboarding timeline and winback contract terms.
playbook-steps: Step 0: Ingest signals (usage, support tickets, billing anomalies, QBR sentiment) into CS Ops dashboard and tag account.
Step 1: Triager (CS Ops or assigned CSM) reviews signals and assigns risk tier within 24 hours.
Step 2: Notify stakeholders: CSM, AE, Solutions Eng, Customer Success Lead, and Finance (for discount approvals) via Slack + email.
Step 3: Run tailored play depending on tier (see mitigation-plans). Document all contact attempts in CRM and link to tix/PRs.
Step 4: If Tier >=3, start 48-hour escalation cadence: prepare exec brief, ROI refresh, tailored POC or feature toggle, and scheduled exec call with 3-day SLA.
Step 5: Post-save: schedule a focused QBR within 30 days with clear success criteria and a 90-day health plan tracked weekly.
Step 6: If save fails, close for churn, capture exit reasons, and queue for winback nurture program.
exec-escalation-template:
Subject: Requesting 30-min Exec Review: [Customer] Renewal in [X days] — Risks & Proposed Fixes

Hi [Customer Exec Name],

I’m the Customer Success Lead for [Customer]. We value our partnership and want to ensure we address a few items prior to your renewal on [renewal date]. We’ve observed a combination of adoption friction, feature gaps, and stakeholder bandwidth constraints that could impact your ROI.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- 30-minute alignment call with our VP/Head of Customer Success
- Share a concise ROI refresh and remediation plan (we’ll deliver within 48 hours)
- Option to trial [feature/SE time/discounted pilot] to validate value in 30 days

We’re committed to making this right — please let us know your availability next week.

Thanks,
[Your name] — Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
mitigation-plans: Light-touch (Tier 1): personalized in-product onboarding checklist, targeted tips emails, 1:1 office hours with CSM, highlight quick wins in the next 14 days.
Medium-touch (Tier 2): AE + SE technical review, ROI recalculation for customer's key workflows, targeted enablement workshops, fast-track bug fixes with Product if blocking adoption.

Heavy-touch (Tier 3): Executive briefing + 'white glove' SE support, temporary pricing incentives (requires Finance approval), dedicated migration/implementation resources, binding 30-day remediation commitments with measurable SLAs.
Survival & Exit (Tier 4): prepare offboarding checklist, capture data export and IP terms, propose structured winback terms and 6-12 month re-engagement plan.
Cross-functional actions: product prioritization ticket, SRE incident review if stability issues involved, legal/finance approval path for concession approvals within 72 hours.
winback-offers: 30-day performance guarantee + service credits if adoption targets not met.
Time-limited discount on annual commit tied to usage milestones.
Free professional services blocks for migration/implementation (up to X hours).
Pilot of new feature or quantization optimization with dedicated SE time to demonstrate cost savings.
metrics-to-track: Time to first response on Tier>=2 signal
Change in core usage (tokens per active user) 30/60/90 days
NPS / CSAT delta from last QBR
% of escalations that convert to saved renewals
QBR-template-snippet:
QBR Agenda snippet for at-risk customers:
- 5m: Exec summary (health, adoption, risk score)
- 10m: ROI update and value realized to date
- 15m: Blockers and remediation plan (owners + timelines)
- 10m: Proposed commitment options (if renewal approaching)
- 5m: Decision & next-steps (schedule follow-up)
Embed the risk tier and action checklist in the QBR doc so execs see the escalation plan live.
slack-templates: @cs-leads FYI: Flagged [Customer] as Tier 3 — renewal [date]. Running exec escalation. TLDR: adoption down 35%, 2 Sev2 tickets open. Requesting VP availability for customer call this week.
@finance Quick approval request: up to 15% concession for [Customer] if they sign 12mo commit by [date]. Jira: JIRA-CS-4127
sample-crm-notes: 2026-02-15: Tier assigned = 2. Customer reduced usage; AE to deliver ROI refresh by 2026-02-18.
2026-02-18: SE workshop scheduled 2026-02-22. CSM to capture outcome and update health score.
post-save-play: If renewal is secured, require a '90-day success plan' owner and weekly health check-ins for the first 90 days. Capture outcome metrics and include in next QBR. If partial renewal, lock in a technical remediation roadmap with timelines and Product SLAs.
next-steps: Share with CS team for feedback and tag any missing play examples. Pilot this runbook on 10 accounts with renewals in the next 90 days and iterate weekly. Add triggers to CS Ops dashboard: weekly active users, Sev2 open time, NPS delta, and procurement signal. Update page when pilot results are in.
notes: This is a living document — keep examples of actual email threads and anonymized post-mortems attached in Confluence. Avoid committing concession amounts without Finance approval. Reach out to CS Ops for automated tags in CRM.
